guitar.evidence: Buddy Holly's sunburst Fender Stratocaster is one of the most iconic and widely documented guitars in early rock and roll history.

tone.summary: A bright, clean signal chain emphasizing twang and vintage slapback echo, mimicking a classic Fender-style rockabilly sound.

rig.name: Buddy Holly - Peggy Sue Got Married - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray noise from the guitar signal.
Slightly boost the signal to maintain presence and cut through the mix.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used for general tone shaping, as a dedicated clean preamp (like an American Deluxe) might be too much. This keeps the initial sound bright.

blocks.purpose: Keep the signal clean and transparent, avoiding any grit or distortion.
Simulate the clean, bright tone of a Fender-style amplifier.
Provide a bright and articulate cabinet sound suitable for twangy lead lines.
Placeholder. Disabled to avoid the forbidden chorus effect.
blocks.gap: The Chorus module is explicitly avoided by the user's requirements and kept inactive.

blocks.purpose: Keep the wah pedal bypassed to maintain a pure, twangy tone.
blocks.gap: The WAH module is kept inactive/bypassed as it is not required for this style.

blocks.purpose: Provide the required short, vintage slapback echo effect.
Add a subtle, natural ambience (light spring feel) without sounding like big reverb.
blocks.gap: Room is used instead of Spring/Plate to achieve the 'light ambience' while avoiding excessive wetness or modern sound.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the short tape echo effect mentioned in the clues.
blocks.gap: Tape is used for its vintage character and ability to provide a subtle, non-washy delay/echo feel.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the default IR for a vintage, bright-sounding speaker to better capture the rockabilly twang.

proposals.reason: Enhance classic Fender/rockabilly brightness and articulation.
